dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Greg.
Hi, yes, good morning. Um, I'm hoping I have the right department. I want to put up a fence, you know, and I'm not sure if I need some kind of permit for that. Is this the place?
Yep, this is the place. Tell me what you've got in mind.
Okay, so, it's not a big thing. It's just a short decorative fence in the front yard, right? Like along the walkway side, just for looks. Nothing to keep anybody in or out.
Okay. How tall are you thinking, and what's it made of?
So it would be black aluminum, and I think, I mean, the one I liked in the catalog is six feet tall. Is that, you know, tall? Does that sound tall for a front yard?
Six feet in a front yard is on the tall side, yeah. Most places keep front yard fences a lot lower than what you'd put in a back yard.

Oh. Okay. So, right, that's what I was wondering. Is there a height where a fence stops needing a permit? Like under a certain number you don't need one and over it you do? Because my sister-in-law said under four feet you're fine, but I don't know if that's, you know, a real rule or just something she heard.

I wouldn't go by a single number somebody told you. In general, a fence in the city is something you should expect to need a permit for, and the front yard is where they look hardest. So the safe answer is to assume yes, you need one, and we confirm it when you apply.
So even a short one, a little decorative one, would still need a permit? Not just the tall ones?
I'd plan on it, yes. Rules on height can differ by where the fence goes on the lot and what zone you're in. That's why I'd rather look at your actual property than hand you a number over the phone.
Right, right. Okay. But then the six feet, that might not even be allowed in front, is that what you're saying?
It may not be, no. Might have to come down in height. Better to find that out now than after you've ordered the aluminum.
Oh, good point, I haven't ordered anything yet. Thank goodness. Um, so what do I do, do I fill something out? Is there a form?

There's a permit application. You can pick one up here at City Hall or find it on the city website under zoning and inspections. You'll want a rough sketch of the lot showing where the fence goes, plus the height and the material.
A sketch, okay. Like a drawing? I'm not an artist, you know.
Doesn't need to be pretty. A simple drawing of the property lines, the house, and a line where the fence runs. Label the measurements.
Okay, I can do that. And, I mean, how long does it take? Like once I turn it in, how long till somebody says yes or no?
It depends how busy we are and whether the application is complete. Usually it's a matter of days to a couple of weeks. If something's missing, it takes longer because we have to come back to you.
Days to a couple weeks. Okay. Because I was hoping to get it in before the, you know, the spring gets going. Right, so that's not terrible.
Shouldn't be. Get the application in complete and you'll save yourself time.

Okay. Now, the website, I should tell you, the print on those forms is always so small. I use a magnifier app on my phone to read the fine print, you know, hold it up and it blows it up. So if I'm looking at the website I'll be fine, I just wanted to say that in case it's tiny.
That works. On the website you can zoom in on the PDF too. And if you come in, we have printed copies, and I can walk you through the boxes.

Oh, that's good. Okay. So, let me just check that I have this right. I need a permit, probably, even for a short one. Six feet in the front might be too tall. I draw a sketch, fill out the form, and it takes days to a couple weeks. Is that right?
That's it. And when you fill out the form, put the real height you want and let the reviewer tell you if it needs to change.
Okay. And I don't need to give you an address right now or anything?
Not for general questions. The address goes on the application. If you want to talk about your specific lot, call back or stop in with it.
Okay, I think I'll do that. I'm still a little, um, not sure about the front yard thing versus the side, but I guess they'll tell me.
They will. Front is stricter, that's all I'd say for now. Anything else?
No, I think that's it. Thank you, Greg. Sorry if I asked it a few different ways.
No problem. Have a good day.
You too, bye.
